label: December 21–27
title: “We Have Waited for Him, and He Will Save Us” —  Christmas

items.text: The Old Testament carries a spirit of eager anticipation, much like the Christmas season. Beginning with Adam and Eve, prophets and people looked forward to better days, filled with hope for the Messiah’s renewal and deliverance, who would “proclaim liberty to the captives.” (Isaiah 61:1)
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: That hope began to be realized when Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem. He came not only to deliver ancient Israel, but to deliver you—to bear your grief, carry your sorrows, and be bruised for your iniquities, so that by His stripes you can be healed. (Isaiah 53:4–5)
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Christmas is known as a joyful season because of the joy that Jesus Christ brings to the world. Centuries before His birth, Old Testament prophets also felt joy as they spoke of the coming Messiah, reminding people of the hope for His mission. (Isaiah 25:8–9)
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Many traditions associated with Christmas can have symbolic meanings that point us to Christ. The Old Testament is filled with symbols of the Savior, such as the star, the shepherd, the lamb, water, the rock, the branch, and light, all testifying of Him.
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The star, a symbol of the Savior, is found in Old Testament prophecies, like in Numbers 24:17, pointing to His coming. This symbol continues in the New Testament, signifying His birth and guiding wise men to Him. (Matthew 2:2; Revelation 22:16)
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Jesus Christ is our Shepherd, guiding and protecting us. Like the shepherd in Psalm 23, He cares for His flock. He is the Good Shepherd who lays down His life for His sheep, offering comfort and direction. (Luke 15:4–7; John 10:11)
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: The lamb is a powerful symbol of Jesus Christ, representing His atoning sacrifice. As the lamb was offered in ancient Israelite traditions, so Christ was the Lamb of God, slain for our sins, allowing us to be redeemed. (Genesis 22:8; Exodus 12:5; 1 Peter 1:18–20)
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Jesus Christ is the living water, offering spiritual refreshment and everlasting life. Like water quenches thirst, His gospel satisfies the soul. He said, “Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.” (John 4:14)
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: Jesus Christ is our Rock, our foundation of truth and strength. He is the sure foundation upon whom we can build our lives. In Him, we find security and stability, even amidst life’s storms. (1 Samuel 2:2; Isaiah 28:16; Ephesians 2:20)
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026

items.text: He is the Light of the world, guiding us through darkness and showing us the way. His teachings illuminate our path and bring hope to our lives. We can turn to Him for direction and to dispel shadows of doubt. (Psalm 27:1; Isaiah 9:2; John 8:12)
items.attribution: Come, Follow Me—For Home and Church: Old Testament 2026
